prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues.

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred third name from Ciulli to Handa. The scientific case for B056 is unchanged: recruiting an E3 ligase into a ternary complex turns occupancy-based inhibition into event-driven, catalytic removal, with quantitative cooperativity and turnover, reproduced independently for about twenty-five years across target classes. What changed is how I weigh the exact credit. My round-1 citation mentioned glue-type molecules while naming no one for the glue strand, and the chair's questions made that inconsistency plain. If the citation rests on the principle of induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases, each name should stand on a distinct, datable discovery: the PROTAC concept and first proof of principle (Crews, Deshaies) and the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (Handa), which explains the molecular glues and most clinical degraders. Ciulli's VHL-ligand and ternary-complex work is the part I value most as a physical chemist, but I now agree with Peter Brzezinski that it reads as a deep line of work building on the concept more than a separate founding step. The expert report should still record how much of the cooperativity framework is Ciulli's, and the citation can say 'from the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism' without naming every contributor. With this move the Crews, Deshaies, Handa configuration has five explicit supporters, but that is not why I moved: I did so because it gives the more coherent citation.
statement.case_against: Three seats cannot cover everyone with a real claim. Ciulli, Sakamoto (2001 co-author), Ito (cereblon with Handa), Gray and Kim are all defensible, and dropping Ciulli leaves out the quantitative structural basis of ternary-complex design, which is where the chemistry is most physical. A single citation spanning PROTACs and cereblon glues may also blur two lineages, as Somfai and Chabes note. No degrader is yet a broadly approved therapy, so part of the impact is still prospective. I would rest the citation on the chemical principle and independent reproduction, not on clinical outcomes, and I accept that the committee must state openly what the three-name limit costs.

responses.point: Peter argues that Crews, Deshaies and Handa is the cleanest attribution because each name rests on a distinct, datable discovery, whereas Ciulli's VHL and ternary-complex work reads as a strong line of work and not a single attributable discovery.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me. In round 1 I put Ciulli ahead because his work supplies the quantitative design level, but a prize should credit a discovery that can be dated and described in one sentence, and the cereblon identification can be, while the cooperativity framework developed over years in several laboratories is harder to isolate. I still ask that the expert report separate what is Ciulli's from what is shared with the Crews laboratory, as Peter requested, so the citation does not understate the structural work. I also agree that naming Handa has a cost: it makes the citation cover two discoveries, which I think is defensible only if the wording is about recruiting ligases to remove proteins and not about PROTACs alone.

responses.point: Heiner prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a bifunctional-molecule citation, but says he can be persuaded that cereblon was the more decisive original step and would add 'induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases' so both strands fit.
responses.response: I stood with Heiner on Ciulli in round 1 and I now think his own proposed wording points the other way. A citation about induced proximity to ligases is incomplete if the molecular glues are described in it but no one who found how they work is credited, and thalidomide-cereblon is the best-known and most consequential case of that principle. I would not oppose a Ciulli trio on scientific grounds, since the cooperativity physics is real and is what drew me to B056, but I think the Handa configuration has a better-defined chain of credit. If Heiner still prefers Ciulli, I would ask what dated discovery he would cite for him, which answers the chair's question on evidence.

responses.point: Daniel holds that including Handa ties the PROTAC strand to the cereblon mechanism so one citation covers both strands, and he would not split B056 into separate parts unless no unified citation can be agreed.
responses.response: I agree and I withdraw my earlier suggestion that cereblon is more naturally a separate achievement. A designed, generalisable concept and the discovery of a target mechanism for an existing drug are different kinds of contribution, but they converge on one principle, ligase recruitment to remove a chosen protein, and a unified citation expresses that better than two parts, which would also use up a second part on one field. I would only add that Daniel's wording 'from the PROTAC concept to the molecular mechanism of thalidomide-type glues' should be kept in the final citation, since it makes the two strands and their order explicit.

responses.point: Xiaodong prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, notes that taking Handa would displace Ciulli, and asks whether Sakamoto should be credited as a 2001 co-author, grounding her support in determined structures.
responses.response: I share her insistence on structural evidence, and I think the cereblon case meets it: the crystal structures of cereblon with thalidomide-type molecules and neosubstrates explain the mechanism of the glue strand at atomic level. On Sakamoto, I do not see a claim strong enough to displace Crews or Deshaies, because the 2001 concept paper is the shared basis of their credit and the three-name limit forces a choice at the level of the lead laboratories. I accept that this is a judgment call and not a settled fact, and I leave it to the expert report on priority to say if the record contradicts it.

responses.point: Peter Somfai prefers B051 (Pd-catalysed C-N coupling) with Buchwald and Hartwig, stresses the clean two-name credit, and says he would move toward B056 if the committee wants to reward a modality rather than a method.
responses.response: The clarity of credit in B051 is a real strength, and I take the point that C-N coupling is a different bond construction from the 2010 prize. I still weigh the recent cross-coupling recognition and Kosugi's precedent against it, and I think B056 is the stronger case for this year because it opens a new kind of control over biology, not a more general version of an established reaction. Peter is not asking for a modality prize, so I would phrase my preference as one about concept and not modality: I find the principle of event-driven removal more novel than the method of amine arylation.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports on priority support Handa over Ciulli for the third seat, and whether Ito or Sakamoto should displace any name.
Whether one citation covering both PROTACs and cereblon glues can be worded without blurring two lineages.
Whether the committee accepts twenty-five years of independent reproduction as maturity while no degrader is yet a broadly approved therapy; I am recalling clinical status, not verifying it.

If B056 does not reach five votes for one trio, whether B024 (phase separation) or B052 (lipid nanoparticles) should be the second part, given the open question of in vivo relevance for B024 and the overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for B052.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. I have no personal, mentoring or institutional tie to any credited name on B056. My research on lipid self-assembly and membranes is close to the lipid nanoparticle topic (B052), which I list only as an alternative, and I would recuse from deciding it if it advanced as a prize part. Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai are Lund colleagues and Daniel Aili's research overlaps scientifically with mine; these are collegial connections and not ties to any shortlisted candidate.
